messages:
maya: Quick FYI — int8 canary (raven-lite-q4a) turned up a streaming-only funcall parse bump, ~+1.9% in the window.
oliver: streaming only? logs?
sam: yeah, non-streaming/gRPC fine. logs show stream flush chopping inside JSON array suffix. sample snippet:
```
..."actions": [{"name":"lookup", "args": {...}} ,
<STREAM_CUTOFF>
```
parser receives truncated object and fails
maya: looks like batching + ratecap burst interaction in the streamer
sophia: could also be kv-cache/prefix alignment but pattern points to flush boundary. two quick mitigations: 1) sentinel terminator token appended to prompt and stripped client-side; 2) reduce streaming batch_max_tokens by ~20% for funcall routes
oliver: sentinel is fastest to test. runtime flush detection (pattern based) is better long term but needs perf bench
sam: repro used:
```
rcli canary run --model raven-lite-q4a --mode streaming --qps 30 --dur 10m --payload samples/fncall-heavy.json
```
maya: ran sentinel canary (~20k req): parse fails dropped from 3.2% -> 0.6%, token usage +0.8%
oliver: small token delta is acceptable if reliability improves. ensure strip happens before tool invoke
sophia: reduced-batch canary also ran: failures down ~60% and token delta ~+0.2% — smaller cost impact
maya: plan: run two parallel canaries (sentinel vs reduced-batch) and collect metrics: funcall_parse_fail, p99-token-loss, token_delta, cpu_alloc. post results to s3
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/stream-sentinel-v0.1 -> canary cluster
sam: results uploaded s3://redwood-canaries/6176543210/results.json
maya: summary: sentinel best for reliability but small cost hit; reduced-batch is good compromise. next step: prototype runtime smart-flush (pattern detect) and perf bench, file follow-up phab ticket
oliver: filed phab T17222 for runtime flush + bench
sophia: also request adding monitor alert: funcall_parse_rate delta >0.5% over baseline
maya: noted and adding to canary playbook/retro :white_check_mark:
